Actually chords connecting opposite quadrants (i.e., quadrants that are opposite across the origin, like Q1 and Q3) are all lines crossing the origin region, but they might intersect each other? For chords connecting Q1 to Q3, the endpoints are in Q1 and Q3. In terms of angular positions, Q1 corresponds to angles between 0 and π/2 (if we define Q1 as first quadrant: 0 < θ < π/2). Q3 corresponds to angles between π and 3π/2 (i.e., π < θ < 3π/2). So any point in Q1 has angle between 0 and π/2; any point in Q3 has angle between π and 3π/2. So any chord connecting a point in Q1 to a point in Q3 will pass through the interior, and two such chords will intersect if the angular order of endpoints is interleaved: i.e., for chords (A in Q1, B in Q3) and (C in Q1, D in Q3), they intersect if and only if the endpoints are interleaved: i.e., as we go around the circle, we see A (Q1), then C (Q1) maybe?
